scope: Grid-code active-power regulation (set-point tracking, ramp rates, curtailment commands from the park / grid operator) at turbine level.
Grid option without a milestone in the Tuning Procedure: confirm whether it is needed for the prototype.
kpi: - Tracking of the active-power set point and ramp rates within the grid-code tolerances.
- No adverse interaction with the speed controllers (speed / pitch transients on set-point changes).
dlcs: **High:** power set-point steps and ramps (curtailment / release).
affects: Active power reference (Reduction Interface) and, through it, the speed controllers.
affected_by: Park controller / grid-operator commands.
risk: Grid-code non-compliance; speed and pitch transients when the set point changes quickly.

tasks.name: Rotor Performance Data
scope: Rotor power and thrust coefficient tables (as a function of wind speed, rotor speed and pitch) used to calculate the wind speed estimate and the thrust estimate (and the available power).
kpi: - Tables consistent with the aerodynamic model of the final blade (power and thrust per operating point).
- Estimators unbiased when fed with these tables (DLC 1.2a).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a and power-curve runs (estimate accuracy over the operating range).
**Medium:** DLC 1.7 OWI (iced rotor deviates from the tables).
affects: - **Wind Speed Estimator**, **Thrust Estimator**, **Power Estimator**, Power Boost, Inertial Response (all use the rotor performance tables).
affected_by: Blade aerodynamics (physical): tables generated from the aeroelastic model.
risk: Wrong tables: biased wind and thrust estimates in every function scheduled on them (speed-pitch gains, HWO, ACS, GILL).

tasks.name: Ice Detector
scope: Detects ice on the blades (from the ice-detection system and turbine signals) because iced blades change the aerodynamics and can throw ice: the turbine is stopped or operated according to the ice-handling type.
Implemented in the legacy STC1 controller.
kpi: - Detection of iced conditions and no false detections; correct hand-over to Operation with Ice.
affects: Operation with Ice (mode selection), stops for ice.
affected_by: Ice sensors, Low Power Detector, the IceDeTyp / DeIceTyp type selections.
risk: Ice not detected: ice throw risk and loads with iced rotor. False detections: availability loss.

tasks.name: No Cut In Detector
scope: Detects when the turbine is not connected to the grid and producing power as expected at a given wind speed (e.g. ice, faults preventing cut-in), and raises the corresponding alarm / ice handling.
kpi: - Detection of a missing cut-in within the expected time at a given wind; no false detections at low wind or during normal start-up delays.
dlcs: **High:** start-up conditions (DLC 3.x wind range) and iced conditions (DLC 1.7 / idling with ice).
affects: Alarms and ice handling (availability).
affected_by: Wind speed measurement, start-up sequence (Operation), DeIceTyp type selection.
risk: False alarms: unnecessary stops. Missed detection: turbine idle without reason or iced rotor not handled.

tasks.name: Power Consumption Monitor
scope: Disabled in normal operation; enabled when the rotor is motored (rotor positioning, generator-driven turning) to protect against excessive power consumption from the grid.
kpi: - Power-consumption limit consistent with the motoring operations of the new rotor (inertia, aerodynamic drag).
affects: Motoring operations (stop when the consumption is too high).
affected_by: Power measurement and the motoring mode (converter / service functions).
risk: Limit too low: motoring aborted (service delays). Too high: overload of the drivetrain / converter while motoring.

tasks.name: Speed Source Interface
scope: Selects which rotor and generator speed signals are used throughout the controller (primary / secondary sources, quality), computes 1 s averages and the low-speed-side generator speed, and disables invalid sources (e.g. on drivetrain oscillation).
kpi: - Correct source selection for the installed sensors and correct fallback when a source fails.
- Delay and noise of the selected speed (affects every speed-based loop).
dlcs: **High:** speed-sensor failure cases (DLC 2.1i and speed-sensor faults).
affects: - **Rotor Speed Filter** (raw speed), **Overspeed Monitor** (1 s averages), **ADTD2** (generator speed LSS), Wind Speed / Thrust Estimators, ACS, monitors: every speed consumer.
affected_by: - Installed speed sensors and their validation; Drive Train Oscillation Monitor (disables a source).
risk: Wrong source or fallback: wrong or delayed speed in every loop, overspeed protection on a bad signal.

tasks.name: Blade Moment Monitor
scope: Detects faulty or wrongly calibrated blade-root moment signals by comparing the blades with each other (flap and edge imbalances, offsets) per revolution, and sets the blade-load status used by the load handles.
kpi: - Imbalance thresholds above the normal blade-to-blade scatter (no false faults) and below the calibration error that would harm the load handles.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.1i / 2.4i blade-sensor failure and replication (the faults it must detect).
**Medium:** DLC 1.2a (normal imbalance from shear, turbulence, pitch errors).
affects: - **Blade Edge Frequency Monitor** (edge moments and status) and, through the blade status, the load handles using blade moments (BLL, GILL, IPC, TTCC, PDA) and the Controller Safe Mode.
affected_by: - Blade Load Sensor Driver / calibration, Rotor Azimuth Estimator (status), Wind Speed Estimator.
risk: Too tight: false sensor faults (load handles off, safe mode, AEP). Too loose: load handles act on wrong moments.

tasks.name: Reverse Rotor Speed Monitor
scope: Prevents problems when the rotor runs in the reverse direction (e.g. idling in low wind from behind): counts reverse rotations from the rotation-direction estimate and acts before they cause damage.
kpi: - Detection of reverse rotation with no false detections at near-zero speed.
dlcs: **High:** idling / parked cases with wind from the back (DLC 6.x with large yaw error).
affects: Stops / actions on reverse rotation.
affected_by: - **Rotor Sensor Fusion:** rotation direction (RSF_RotDirSt, main input).
risk: Missed reverse rotation: damage to bearings / gearbox lubrication. False detections: unnecessary alarms.

tasks.name: Drive Train Oscillation Monitor (DTOM)
scope: Prevents critical drivetrain oscillations: it band-pass filters the speed signals around the drivetrain modes and stops the turbine (or disables a speed source) when the oscillation exceeds the limits.
kpi: - Limits above the oscillation levels of normal operation and grid faults (no nuisance stops) and below critical levels; band-pass frequencies on the drivetrain modes of the new design.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.5a LVRT / DLC 2.1g (torque steps excite the drivetrain); DLC 1.2a (normal levels).
affects: - **Speed Source Interface:** DTOMx__Disable invalidates an oscillating speed source; turbine stops.
affected_by: - Speed signals and the drivetrain modes (physical); ADTD2 (damping reduces the oscillation levels).
risk: Too tight: nuisance stops after grid faults. Too loose: drivetrain damage from sustained oscillation.

tasks.name: Blade Edge Frequency Monitor
scope: Monitors the blade edgewise frequency of each blade (from blade edge moments or accelerations, with azimuth and whirling correction) and detects significant changes that indicate blade damage, then stops the turbine.
kpi: - Normal scatter of the estimated edge frequency (temperature, ice, operating point) vs the change threshold: no false alarms; detection of the frequency drop that indicates damage.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a over the operating range (natural frequency variation).
affects: Stops for blade inspection (structural safety, availability).
affected_by: - **Blade Moment Monitor** (edge moments and blade status, main input), Rotor Azimuth Estimator, Rotor Speed Filter (whirling frequency only).
- Blade structural properties (physical).
risk: Too tight: false stops. Too loose: blade damage not detected.

tasks.name: Blade Flapwise Vibration Monitor (BFVM)
scope: Prevents the blades from reaching a critical flapwise vibration level (increased fatigue or, in the worst case, instability): on high vibration it adds a pitch offset and reduces the speed, and stops if needed.
kpi: - Vibration limits above normal operation levels and below critical levels; effectiveness of the pitch offset / speed reduction.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a / 1.3 (normal and extreme flap vibration levels).
affects: - **Pitch Trajectory Offsets:** BldFlpVb__PitOff; **Reduction Interface:** BldFlpVb__SpdRed (speed reduction).
affected_by: Blade flap measurements and Speed-Pitch Controller (event data).
risk: Too tight: unnecessary derating. Too loose: blade fatigue or flap instability.

tasks.name: Order Tracker
scope: Estimates the 1P, 2P and 3P amplitudes over time in important signals (e.g. generator speed), tracking the rotor orders as the speed changes; the Order Tracker Monitor uses them to detect rotor imbalance or drivetrain issues.
kpi: - Amplitude estimates vs the order content of the simulated signals; stable estimates over the speed range.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a (order content in normal operation; rotor imbalance cases if simulated).
affects: - **Order Tracker Monitor:** 2P / nP amplitudes of the generator speed (alarms).
affected_by: Speed signals, gear ratio (GearType) and the rotor speed.
risk: Wrong tracking: false imbalance / drivetrain alarms or missed detection.

tasks.name: Power Inflow Estimator
scope: Estimates the aerodynamic power flowing into the rotor from the electrical power and the change of rotational kinetic energy (rotor inertia x speed x acceleration), so that the wind estimate is not disturbed by speed transients.
kpi: - Power-inflow estimate vs the aerodynamic power of the simulation, especially during speed transients.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a and DLC 1.4 (speed transients where electrical power differs from aerodynamic power).
affects: - **Wind Speed Estimator:** PwrInflow_PwrEst as power input (and through it every wind-scheduled function).
affected_by: Electrical power, rotor speed / acceleration and the rotor-system inertia (physical).
risk: Wrong inertia: biased wind estimate during accelerations (gain scheduling, HWO, ACS).

tasks.name: Speed Measurement Validator
scope: Validates each rotor-speed measurement source (hub, main shaft, generator, converter, safety-system sensors) and provides its status, so that only valid sources are used.
kpi: - Correct detection of failed or implausible sources with no false invalidations.
affects: - **Rotor Sensor Fusion:** status of each source (which sources are fused).
affected_by: Installed speed sensors (physical).
risk: False invalidation: degraded speed estimate; missed fault: bad source used for control and protection.

tasks.name: Gearbox Slip Monitor
scope: Prevents the generator side and the rotor side of the drivetrain from slipping relative to each other (slip in the gearbox / shaft connection), which would introduce high loads, by comparing the two speeds / angles.
kpi: - Slip limit above the normal torsional deflection and measurement differences; detection of real slip.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.5a / 2.1g (large torque steps: largest torsional deflection).
affects: Turbine stops on slip (drivetrain protection).
affected_by: Rotor-side and generator-side speed / angle measurements, gear ratio, drivetrain stiffness (physical).
risk: Too tight: false stops after torque transients. Too loose: drivetrain damage not detected.

tasks.name: Rotor Performance Monitor
scope: Detects when the rotor does not perform as expected (wind-speed estimate vs measured wind, e.g. ice or blade degradation); currently in observer mode.
kpi: - Detection thresholds above the normal scatter between estimated and measured wind; detection of iced or degraded rotors.
affects: Performance / ice information (observer mode: no control action).
affected_by: - **Wind Speed Estimator** (filtered estimate and status), wind measurement, Operation with Ice (external ice sensor data).
risk: Observer mode: wrong thresholds only produce wrong information, no control action.

tasks.name: Speed Mismatch Monitor
scope: Identifies mismatches between the rotor-speed measurements of different sources (e.g. rotor vs generator speed through the gear ratio) and raises alarms, so that a faulty sensor or drivetrain problem is detected.
kpi: - Mismatch limits above normal differences (torsional dynamics, measurement noise) and below fault levels.
dlcs: **High:** speed-sensor failure cases and DLC 2.5a / 2.1g (torsional transients create apparent mismatch).
affects: Alarms / source handling (Speed Source Interface).
affected_by: Speed sources and their selection.
risk: Too tight: false alarms after transients. Too loose: faulty speed sensor not detected.

tasks.name: Blade Edgewise Vibration Monitor (BEVM)
scope: Prevents the blades from reaching a critical edgewise vibration level (fatigue or, in the worst case, edgewise instability): it band-pass filters the blade edge signals around the edgewise modes and, above the limits, adds a pitch offset, reduces the speed or stops the turbine.
kpi: - Vibration limits above the normal edgewise levels in operation and idling, and below critical levels.
- Effectiveness of the pitch offset / speed reduction on the edgewise vibration.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 6.x idling and parked with large yaw / inflow angles (edgewise vibration risk is highest in standstill and idling); DLC 1.7 OWI and 1.2a.
affects: - **Pitch Trajectory Offsets:** OffPitch_EdgVbMon; **Reduction Interface:** GSVibrat__SpdRed (speed reduction); stops.
affected_by: - Blade edge moments / accelerations, Speed Source Interface (rotor speed for the 1P band-stop), Speed-Pitch Controller (pitch-angle compensation and event data).
- Blade edgewise modes (physical).
risk: Too tight: unnecessary derating / stops. Too loose: edgewise vibrations not stopped (blade damage).

tasks.name: High Temperature Ride Through (HTRT)
scope: Extends the operational area at high ambient temperatures: instead of stopping when components get hot, the turbine is derated (power reduction) based on thermal models of the electrical components; it can also enable a speed boost in curtailment.
kpi: - Component temperatures within limits with the derating; production kept instead of stops at high temperature.
dlcs: **High:** high-temperature operation scenarios (not a load DLC; thermal cases).
affects: - **Reduction Interface:** HTRTCtrl__PRedDera (power derating); **Power Boost:** speed-boost activation.
affected_by: - Component temperatures and thermal models (HTRTType selects the configuration), rated / design power.
risk: Derating too late: component over-temperature and trips. Too early: AEP loss in hot climates.

tasks.name: Rotor Speed Filter
scope: Filters the measured rotor speed and rotor acceleration with a chain of band-stop (notch) filters at 3P, 6P, the 1st-3rd edgewise symmetric frequencies (1ES-3ES, centre frequencies estimated online by ESFE) and the tower 2nd mode (from the Tower Frequency Estimator), a generic band-stop, a low-pass and a lead filter.
Goal: remove the harmonic and structural content that would excite the control loops and the structure, without adding phase delay that degrades the speed control.
kpi: - Phase delay and gain of the filter chain (with and without lead filter) at the speed-loop crossover frequency.
- Attenuation of the rotor-speed spectrum at 3P, 6P, 1ES-3ES and the tower 2nd frequency, before vs after (DLC 1.2a).
- [P] Rotor speed std / max per wind bin (DLC 1.2a) and speed peak in gusts (DLC 1.4, 9.4w) not worse than the reference.
- [P] Pitch activity (RMS pitch rate) and fatigue of blade-root edgewise, pitch bearing, drivetrain and tower-base fore-aft in DLC 1.2a.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a normal turbulence (the rotor-speed spectrum carries 3P, edgewise and tower content; whatever passes the filters becomes pitch and torque activity and fatigue of pitch bearings, blades and drivetrain); DLC 1.4 ECD and DLC 9.4w extreme ECD with turbulence (the gust response of the speed loop depends on the phase of the filtered speed; ACS and the controller overspeed monitor are disabled, so the speed loop alone drives the tower and blade extremes).

**Medium:** DLC 2.1g grid drop and DLC 2.5a LVRT (torque is lost and the rotor accelerates fast: filter delay increases the speed peak seen by the speed-pitch loop and GFRT); DLC 1.3 ETM (large speed excursions in extreme turbulence).
**Lower:** DLC 1.2 NTM (baseline robustness); DLC 1.7 OWI (ice mass lowers the blade edgewise frequencies: the notches must follow the ESFE estimate).
affects: - **Speed-Pitch Controller:** RotSpdFi_SpdLead is the speed feedback of the PI (speed error, reference saturation and ramping) and, low-pass filtered, a gain-scheduling input: filter phase and lead gain set the loop margin and the gust response.
- **Speed-Power Controller:** RotSpdFi_Spd is its PI feedback and gain-scheduling input; RotSpdFi_SpdLead selects the operating point on the active power envelope.

- **Converter Interface:** RotSpdFi_Spd converts the power reference into the generator torque reference and the electrical limits: filter delay or residual ripple appears directly in the torque and the drivetrain loads.
- **Resonance Speed Avoider:** the RSA state machine and the window speed references use the filtered speed: delay causes late window crossings and more time near the tower resonance.
- **ESFE:** SpdFilt_nPGnrcSpd is the signal ESFE estimates the edgewise frequencies from (closed loop with the 1ES-3ES notches).
- **Grid Fault Ride Through** (state machine and speed-pitch gain scaling during grid faults) and Power Control States (speed-dependent stop ramp).

**Only scheduling or nP frequency** (they need the correct mean speed, not the filter dynamics): ADTD2 (3P notch frequency and lead-factor scheduling; its damping algorithm uses the unfiltered GenSdSpd_ValueLSS), Active Tower Damper Side-Side (gain proportional to rotor speed), BLL (3P dead-band), GILL (3P / 6P / 9P tracking notches on the blade moments; the RotAcc type that would use RotAccFi__Acc is disabled), IPC and TTCC (3P frequency, azimuth shift), Nacelle Acceleration Filter (nP tracking notches), PDA (speed activation level).
The Controller Overspeed Monitor (listed in the Jira example) does not use the filtered speed: it monitors the 1 s averages of the Speed Source Interface.
affected_by: - **Speed Source Interface:** RotSpd_Value is the raw speed entering the filter chain (source selection and its delay).
- **ESFE:** ESFE_Freq1ES-3ES are the centre frequencies of the 1ES-3ES notches; a wrong estimate moves the notch away from the mode.
- **Tower Frequency Estimator:** TwrFrqPr_Freq2nd / Stat2nd place the tower 2nd-mode notch.
- Rotor Sensor Fusion (RSF__RotAcc, rotor acceleration path) and the design rotor speed (3P / 6P notch frequencies).
risk: **Band-stop filters (3P, 6P, 1ES-3ES, tower 2nd):** a mistuned notch lets harmonic or structural content into the pitch and power control: unintended pitch and power contributions, higher pitch bearing damage and excitation of blades, tower and drivetrain (fatigue, reduced lifetime). Too wide notches add phase delay to the speed loop.

**Low-pass filter:** too low a cut-off delays the speed response, reduces stability and can lead to overspeed; too high a cut-off leaves high-frequency content in the speed signal (pitch bearing damage, excitation of blades, tower and drivetrain).

**Lead filter:** too little lead gives delayed, less aggressive pitch reactions to gusts and higher extreme loads (DLC 1.4), especially without LOPC sensors; too much lead amplifies high-frequency content (pitch activity, fatigue).

tasks.name: Speed-Pitch Controller (PI)
scope: Controls the rotor speed with the collective pitch when the turbine is at rated power or at the active power reference: a PI controller with gain scheduling (pitch angle, rotor speed, wind speed) that tracks the speed-pitch set point SpdRefHa.PitSpeed = ActRef.Speed + SpeedShift_Pitch.

Includes a pitch feed-forward on effective power-reference changes, a feed-forward against overspeed during grid faults (gain scaled with the time to the overspeed limit) and a High Speed Gain near the speed limits. Its output PitchRefCollective is the base of every pitch command.
kpi: - Rotor speed mean, std and max per wind bin vs the active reference (DLC 1.2a).
- Overspeed peak (DLC 1.2a, 1.4) and time above the allowed high-speed region (flutter boundary).
- Tower-base fore-aft extreme in DLC 1.4.
- Constraints: pitch activity (RMS and max pitch rate, time at the pitch-rate limit), AEP, tower fore-aft fatigue in DLC 1.2a, no controller or safety overspeed alarm during grid faults (DLC 2.5).
- [P] Gain and phase margins of the linearised loop over the operating range.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a normal turbulence (speed regulation, pitch activity and tower fatigue); DLC 1.4 ECD (the speed peak and the tower fore-aft extreme in a gust depend on the loop bandwidth); DLC 2.5a LVRT and DLC 2.1g grid drop (generator torque is lost, so pitch is the only means to stop the acceleration); DLC 9.4c ECG frontal passage (a sustained gust pushes the speed towards the limits where the High Speed Gain acts).
**Medium:** DLC 1.3 ETM (large speed excursions); DLC 2.4a/b extreme yaw error (skewed inflow lowers the aerodynamic gain the scheduling assumes); DLC 2.1c controller overspeed.
**Lower:** DLC 1.2 NTM (robustness); DLC 1.7 OWI (iced blades change the aerodynamic gain).
affects: - **Pitch Reference Limiter:** saturates and rate-limits each blade reference built on PitchRefCollective (the command sent to the pitch system).
- **Pitch Trajectory Offsets:** the load-handle offsets and minimum-pitch shift are applied on top of PitchRefCollective; MinPitchLimitActive drives the pitch-limit-by-wind logic.
- **IPC:** cyclic pitch on top of the collective; its amplitude limits use the collective pitch.
- **Pitch Control States:** stop-zone pitch-rate limits and the minimum pitch rate (SpdPit_RotSpdErrDsgn).

**Pitch as operating-point / scheduling variable** (their behaviour shifts when the pitch behaviour changes): Wind Speed and Thrust Estimators (aerodynamic tables; their estimates schedule other functions), GILL (gain scheduling of the BLS type), TAL and PDA (activation level), SLCP (speed curtailment from the collective pitch, flutter boundary), Power Trajectory (speed-power curve scaling with SpdPitch__SpdRefSR), Speed Control Scheduler (pitch derivative sets the power / speed ramp rate), RSA (pitch gap buffer), Power Boost criteria, GFRT (ActSpdRefPitCtrl in the gain scaling).
Monitors (overspeed, blade and tower vibration) use PitchRefCollective only for event data.
affected_by: - **Rotor Speed Filter:** RotSpdFi_SpdLead is the speed feedback and a gain-scheduling input.
- **Pitch Servo Controller:** the actuator dynamics are inside the speed loop (physical coupling, no signal link).
- **Wind Speed Estimator:** WinAvail__SpdRotEq is a gain-scheduling input.
- **Resonance Speed Avoider:** RSA_SpdPitchCtrlGain scales the gains and RSA_SpdPitchRef moves the speed reference.
- **Grid Fault Ride Through:** FRTPCtrl__SpdPiGn scales the gains, GFRT_State and GFRT_TimeActPhase drive the grid-fault feed-forward.
- **Overspeed Monitor:** OvSpdMon__TtoLim (time to the active overspeed limit) scales the pitch feed-forward gain.

- Power Control States (EffPwrRefChange feed-forward), Pitch Trip Avoider (feed-forward), Torque Mismatch Detector (gain modification), Pitch Control States (states, pitch limits and ramps), Speed Control Scheduler (forced reference change).
risk: Too soft: larger speed excursions, overspeed peaks, alarms or stops in gusts and grid faults, higher tower fore-aft extremes in DLC 1.4.
Too aggressive: pitch chatter and rate-limit saturation, pitch bearing and actuator damage, higher tower fatigue, interaction with the tower mode.

Gain scheduling not matched to the rotor (aerodynamic sensitivity, inertia): loss of stability margin in parts of the envelope. Grid-fault feed-forward or High Speed Gain mistuned: overspeed alarms during LVRT or near the limits.

tasks.name: Blade Load Limiter (BLL)
scope: Reduces extreme blade flap (out-of-plane) loads and tip deflection, mainly caused by extreme yaw error or turbulence: it estimates the peak out-of-plane moment of each blade and, when it exceeds a load threshold, adds a collective pitch offset to the minimum pitch limit.
Trade-off: a limited, controlled loss of aerodynamic efficiency (design rule: AEP loss at most 0.2 % in DLC 1.2a).
kpi: - Blade-root flap extreme and tip-to-tower clearance in DLC 1.2a / 1.2c and their extrapolation (DLC 1.1).
- AEP loss at most 0.2 % in DLC 1.2a.
- Activation statistics and pitch offset magnitude / duration vs wind speed.
- Robustness to blade-load sensor uncertainty (thresholds x1.08).
- [P] Pitch activity and interaction with PDA, GILL and TTCC (combined pitch offsets).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a normal turbulence and DLC 1.2c steep shear (flap extremes and tip clearance in normal operation, and the extrapolated extremes of DLC 1.1); DLC 1.2b and 1.2c with thresholds x1.08 (blade-load sensor uncertainty: the protection must still work with the measurement error).
**Medium:** DLC 2.4a/b extreme yaw error (large flap moments from skewed inflow, a main BLL driver); DLC 1.3 ETM; DLC 1.5 EWS (shear raises the flap moment of the upper blade).
**Lower:** DLC 1.4 ECD (gust extremes are mainly handled by GILL and TTCC).
affects: - **Pitch Trajectory Offsets:** BLL_PitchOff is combined with the other load offsets and shifts the minimum pitch / PitchRefCollective.
- **Controller Functionality Scheduler:** BLL / PDA prioritisation uses BLL_PitchOff and its rate.
- **Controller Safe Mode:** BLL_Status triggers the safe-mode derating when the blade-load signals are not valid.
- Indirectly the Speed-Pitch Controller (raised minimum pitch) and AEP.
affected_by: - **Moment Transformations:** MomTrans_A/B/COopMom are the out-of-plane moments the peak estimate is built on; MomTStat_* are their status (validity check).
- **Blade Load Sensor Driver / calibration:** absolute thresholds are only meaningful with calibrated blade loads.
- **Speed-Pitch Controller and Pitch Trajectory Tables:** physical coupling: BLL acts on top of the collective pitch and the minimum-pitch baseline, which must be final first.
- Rotor Speed Filter only for the 3P dead-band of the peak estimate.
risk: Threshold too low: unnecessary pitch-out and AEP loss above the design rule. Threshold too high: flap extremes and tip-tower clearance not protected.
Aggressive filter dynamics: unnecessary pitch activity and actuator wear. Adverse interaction with PDA or GILL (compounded pitch-out) and shift of the operating point that raises tower loads.

tasks.name: Gust Induced Load Limiter (GILL)
scope: Mitigates tower fore-aft extreme loads in gusts: it computes a collective pitch offset from positive changes of the average blade out-of-plane moment (BLS type, GILL.AvMomCng) and adds it to the minimum pitch limit. A second type based on rotor acceleration exists but is disabled.
GILL reacts to how fast thrust increases, not to the thrust level: a transient extreme-load function that must not act in normal turbulent operation.
kpi: - Tower-base fore-aft and blade-root extremes in the gust DLCs, GILL on vs off.
- Activation in normal operation: share of time with GILL.PitchOff > 0 per wind bin in DLC 1.2a and the power-curve runs (must be minimal).
- AEP and pitch activity (RMS and max pitch rate).
- Detection timing: GILL.AvMomCng vs the gust front and clean release of the offset.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.4 ECD (a fast thrust rise excites the tower fore-aft mode: the design-driving tower extreme GILL is made for); DLC 2.3 EOG with grid drop (gust plus torque loss: thrust and speed rise together); DLC 9.4 extreme gusts.
**Medium:** DLC 1.2a and the power-curve runs (no activation and no AEP loss in normal turbulence); DLC 3.x start-up with EOG / EDC (gust while the rotor is accelerating); DLC 1.3 ETM.
**Lower:** DLC 1.5 EWS (shear changes are slow compared with a gust front).
affects: - **Pitch Trajectory Offsets:** GILL__PitchOff is combined with the other load offsets and shifts the minimum pitch / PitchRefCollective.
- **Controller Functionality Scheduler:** GILL / PDA prioritisation.
- **Controller Safe Mode:** GILL__BLSSt (BLS status) triggers the safe-mode derating.
- Indirectly the tower response shared with TAL and the Speed-Pitch Controller, and AEP.
affected_by: - **Moment Transformations:** MomTrans_A/B/COopMom form the average out-of-plane moment (after band-stop filtering) whose rate is the GILL detection signal; MomTStat_* are their status.
- **Speed-Pitch Controller:** PitchRefCollective is the gain-scheduling input of the BLS type.
- **Controller Functionality Scheduler:** GILL off flags (status handling).
- Rotor Speed Filter only for the 3P / 6P / 9P tracking notches; Thrust Estimator only for the disabled rotor-acceleration type.
risk: Thresholds too low or filter too fast: activation in normal turbulence, AEP loss and pitch wear. Thresholds too high or filter too slow: delayed response (about 0.1 s penalty in gust cases), tower extremes not shaved.
Poor gain scheduling: uneven load reduction over the wind-speed range. Compounded pitch-out with BLL / PDA if not coordinated.

tasks.name: Controller Overspeed Monitor
scope: Primary protection layer against rotor overspeed: two monitors on the primary and two on the secondary speed source (1 s averages) stop the turbine (Alm116031 waiting / Alm116032 stopped) before critical speeds cause extreme or fatigue loads. The secondary layer is the safety system (SRSG, Alm114041; LMU, Alm114018).
The limits are relative to the active speed reference and dynamic (DynLim01-03); the monitor also provides the time to the active limit and the active limits to other functions.
kpi: - Margin between the thresholds and the maximum 1 s-average rotor speed: low-threshold monitor at least x1.07 over normal turbulence (DLC 1.2 / 1.2a / 1.2c) and x1.05 over extreme turbulence, gusts and shear (DLC 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 9.4c); high-threshold monitor at least x1.02 over grid drop (DLC 2.1g) and x1.05 over LVRT (DLC 2.5).
- Thresholds below the safety system (SRSG / LMU) and the converter overspeed trip, so the controller layer acts first.
- No nuisance overspeed alarm in normal operation; overspeed detected in the overspeed fault case (DLC 2.1c).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.1c controller overspeed (fault case: the monitor must act); DLC 2.1g grid drop and DLC 2.5a LVRT (torque loss gives the highest speed peaks: high threshold); DLC 1.2 / 1.2a / 1.2c, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 and 9.4c (normal and extreme operation must stay below the low threshold).
**Medium:** DLC 2.2 safety-system overspeed (order of the two protection layers).
The controller overspeed monitor is disabled in most load cases, so the loads do not include its stops: the margins are checked with the monitor enabled.
affects: - **Speed-Pitch Controller:** OvSpdMon__TtoLim (time to the active limit) scales the pitch feed-forward gain.
- **Pitch Damage Attenuator:** OvSpdMon__Lim1 sets the rotor-speed activation level.
- **Grid Forming Operator:** OvSpdMon__ActLim defines its overspeed limits.
- Availability and AEP (overspeed stops) and the protection-layer order with the safety system.
affected_by: - **Speed Source Interface:** RotSpdPr__1sAvg and RotSpdSe__1sAvg are the monitored speeds.
- **Reduction Interface:** ActRefSpeedRSA is the reference the adaptive low and high limits are computed from.
- **Grid Fault Ride Through / converter:** GFRT_iDipMode and the converter mode select the limits during grid dips.

- **Speed-Pitch Controller and the load handles** (BLL, GILL, IPC, TTCC, PDA, TAL): physical coupling: they set the speed peaks the margins are measured on (PitchRefCollective itself is only used for alarm event data).
risk: Too low: nuisance overspeed stops (availability, AEP) and extra loads from the stops. Too high: no primary protection; the safety system trips instead (harder stops, higher loads) or the design overspeed is exceeded.
